Most of the time I unplug it from the wall and wave it over the fly to catch it in its stick pad and that’s how I’ve caught 75% of the insects pictured. Outside of the light, theres nothing really special that draws the flies to the trap so I would think about pairing it with an apple cider vinegar trap to lure them in and hope they get stuck in the trap. The video included is how I catch them manually. It seems seem for animals and children and does not emit any smell. As far as quality, I rate it 1-2 stars as a standalone device, 3 stars is because with my fly catching idea, at least it is catching something. It almost makes me want to buy just the refills and have them on standby to catch on my own. I did expect more out of the quality coming from the Zevo brand. It does not kill the bugs, it just makes them stuck until they die. I’ve had this for about 2 - 3 weeks and this is all it’s caught (small bugs on it’s own, larger flies with my assistance).

title: Zevo Flying Insect Traps & 2 Refill Cartridges (first and second version)
body: My two‑star rating reflects an average between the first and second versions of the Zevo trap, because the two products performed very differently. First Version – No Longer Available, and Misleading The original version is no longer listed, so I can’t leave a review specifically for it. If I could, it wouldn’t get more than one star. The main reason I bought it was the claim that it also worked for mosquitoes. After using it for a year and a half, I can confirm that this was completely false. It catches plenty of other flying insects, but never mosquitoes, which made the original purchase pointless for my needs. Second Version – Accurate Description, Works Properly The updated version no longer claims to trap mosquitoes—likely removed after customer complaints. And this time, the product performs exactly as described. For the insects it lists, it works reliably, and I would normally rate this version five stars on its own. Final Rating Logic Because I can’t leave a separate review for the discontinued first version, and because the original misleading claims were the reason I bought the product in the first place, I’m forced to average the experience. I can’t give 2.5 stars, so I’m leaving 2 stars to reflect the accurate performance of the new version and the misleading marketing of the old one.

title: Gnat Busters
body: I gave Zevo these two out of five stars because this trap only catches 2 out of 5 Gnats. I placed two devices where Gnats love to gather. One in the Kitchen, One near the bathroom. I check every day, as I also kill Gnats by hand every day. I have a very clean home; I use a garbage disposal and do not store food that can rot in the kitchen bin. I store all fruit and vegetables in the refrigerator. Yet every time that I leave a door or window open for fresh air, these little critters gather. (Even with screens). I have tried everything. But this was the most expensive and least successful. I will return to flying insect sprays. I do not know what so called "Genius" thought that insects like "blue light." But I do know, he/she is not very intelligent. I also have 2 blue light/ light bulbs, that are also zappers... also no results. My recommendations, keep a clean house, wash and dry all fruit and vegetables and store them appropriately, (never store fruit or any food in open air). And my latest discovery... If you use a citrus dish cleaning liquid, keep the bottle clean and the top tight. It is weird, but I have recently discovered that Gnats are attracted to the artificial scent.

title: It just didn't attract the flying insects as much as was advertised, especially for the price.
body: It's basically expensive fly paper. The blue light is supposed to attract flying bugs and it does - but only mildly. The height of fruit fly season runs from August to October. There were so many fruit flies in my house, it was hard to have a conversation without waiving the little buggers away. Enter Zevo - which I have seen being advertised aggressively on TV as being the greatest flying insect eradicator ever. So I shelled out the money for 2 blue lit insect traps and 2 refill cartridges, assembled, plugged in and sat back waiting for the fruit fly fog to clear. It never did. I broke down and added 2 bowls filled with Apple Cider Vinegar, topped with tightly covered saran wrap, poked some tiny holes in the wrap and watched to see what worked better. Scot 1 for the Apple Cider Vinegar. I collected 100x more fruit flies in 2 days than I did the entire time I had the cartridges plugged in. The blue lights are pretty - I'll give it that. But it's passively effective, not aggressively effective, so I'll continue to use my tried and true, albeit kinda gross, method.

title: More bug nightclub than bug graveyard.
body: It’s gnat season, and after yet another round of vinegar pots, I decided to go high tech with these Zevo plug-in traps. I put one upstairs, one downstairs, and waited for the carnage. In practice? Not much carnage. After a month (and a house so thick with gnats you could smack them out of the air just walking by), I’ve caught… maybe 15. I watch the bugs chilling in the blue light like it’s happy hour, but they refuse to land on the sticky trap. Maybe my gnats are too smart, maybe my walls are extra tasty, or maybe I’m just more attractive than UV. Whatever it is, these things aren’t worth the money or the hassle of a bright blue beacon glowing 24/7 on both floors of my house. To be fair: The design is pretty cool. The sticky refills are easy to replace, and you don’t have to touch the goo. But I could easily catch more bugs with my bare hands in three minutes than these have snagged in three weeks. If the point is to catch bugs, this thing missed the mark. Unless you’re looking to start your own insect sanctuary, I’d keep looking.

body: We have/had a gnat problem in our house. First in the kitchen, and then in the bathroom. I bought a bug zapper for the kitchen, which worked well, but scares the heck out of you every time a bug gets zapped. Sam's also had a rotating bug trap that works pretty well. When the gnats moved to the bathroom, there wasn't enough space away from the sink, toilet, or bathtub to put the zapper. I went ahead and bought these traps to plug in there, as well as the spray that Zevo sells. I figured, given the small footprint of the bathroom, the plug-in trap would be perfect. The first night, it caught two gnats, and I thought, "Great, it works!" However, a week later, the same two gnats were in there, and no additional gnats. Another week, same two gnats. For whatever reason, the "night light" lure just didn't bring in any more gnats. I ended up killing the rest of the gnats either with the spray or with a swatter of some type (mostly my hand). Does it work? Sure, yes. Does it work well? Not really, at least not in my case. I did notice that both Sam's and Costco sell these as well, so I'm guessing they have to be popular enough, right?

title: You can catch more fruit flies with vinegar than you can with ZEVO traps.
body: My garden has been overflowing with tomatoes and summer squash and my counters were accumulating bowls of produce faster than I could can or freeze them. Suddenly I had an infestation of fruit flies. Prior to using ZEVO, I was using an old home remedy for trapping fruit flies. I placed a piece of banana in a jar, covered the opening with plastic wrap, and punched a couple of slits in the plastic wrap. In a second jar I placed pieces of tomato. The fruit flies can get into the jar through the slits but can’t get out. My ZEVO order arrived two days after I set out the jars and I eagerly put the ZEVO traps to work. The next morning I checked the traps. The ZEVO traps had only 5 or 6 fruit flies attached to the sticky trap. The jars which had been sitting out for 2 days, had a dozen or so fruit fries and my counters were still full of flies. The next morning, the ZEVO traps had a few more flies but the jars were full of flies. Now, four days later, the ZEVO traps continue to underperform. I replaced the banana with a little vinegar and it’s like a fruit fly magnet.

title: Did not work for fruit flies- waste of our money
body: So far I am not at all impressed. Not sure how we got them but all of a sudden we had a ton of fruit flies. (Despite no fruit out and rotting. Nothing we could find. Unless they were in the drain….i have no clue where they came from) We did a kitchen and fridge deep clean. We did drain cleaning. Garbage can bleaching. Etc. Bought these. Plugged one in in out kitchen. A few days later…nothing. Not one single fruit fly was caught. Opened and plugged in the second one as well. Two days later….still nothing. I killed more with my hands than these caught. I gave up and called my mom and ended up doing the old wives take ACV and dish soap with plastic wrap and holes in it over it. I have 10 over night that way. Two days later they are all dead in my ACV trap. Too bad these $35 traps couldn’t have caught and killed a single one. Maybe they work better with different bugs than fruit flies but….they absolutely did nothing for us.

title: Zevo fly trap did not work for me
body: Many reviewers praise this fly trap and have had success with it, but my experience has been that the fly trap is very ineffective. I have numerous house flies in my condo, but they ignore the Zevo fly trap and do not seem attracted to the UV light. I have tried placing the fly trap right where the flies are, tried dimming the lights and darkening the room to make the UV light more visible, and have tried moving the trap around to several different locations. None of these approaches work. At the moment, there are approximately 10 flies in my small condo. They fly around and near the trap, but ignore it and do not seem attracted to it at all. For me, this was a fairly expensive investment to help control the flies. I was optimistic it would help based on all the positive reviews, but it did not work for me. I'm already calling it a loss and looking for another alternative.

title: Not very effective for fruit flies
body: I recently went out of town for a week and left the wife on her own. We already had a couple fruit flies when I left (maybe 3-5 that I noticed), but this isn't unusual since we always buy fruit as it comes into season and this brings fruit fly eggs into the house. Before I left I just reminded her that the trap needed to be setup and she said it wouldn't be a problem. By trap, I mean the apple shaped trap you can get at just about any store where you put a little vinegar and dish soap in and it just "makes the problem go away." I have used those traps for years and they work great, I just put one on the table near the fruit bowl and one near the kitchen sink. Well, I get home and it seems the wife stopped doing dishes and taking out the trash for a week and and fruit flies had gone ham in the sink. Absolute infestation. Swarms plume from the sink when you approach it. The little apples couldn't keep up. So I figured I would try something new. The new UV trap has been setup for 4 days/3 nights. The trap is plugged in right next to the kitchen sink and all the lights are off at night so this trap has had the best chance of succeeding. It has caught, a disappointing number of flies. Maybe 15-20 in that number of days when the number in the house is multiple hundred. I actually just before writing this unplugged it and waved it around over the sink and caught 4 time more in 30 seconds waving this thing around than I have in 4 days. This is probably fine as a very minor preventative, but it costs way more than the little apples, is far more noticeable and not any more effective. I do not recommend.

title: Doesn't work or is too slow.
body: Look, the idea of trying to get rid of those annoying fruit flies makes my skin crawl and my blood boil at the same time. I hate them. Most insect such as those I despise. But nothing I hate more than fruit flies. This product took AGES to catch even a couple of them, let alone the thousands that are made per day sometimes. If any of you reading this have had them, you know what I mean. They are obnoxious. Here is the thing: the quicker you kill them off, the better. This will not do it, not even close. Left them on for a month and when I went to just toss them in the garbage, I could literally count the fruit flies and other things that somehow found there way behind this to get stuck. Here is how you get rid of fruit flies MUCH QUICKER and for WAY LESS MONEY: Apple cider vinegar + ramekin or other small/medium container + clear plastic wrap + toothpick. Fill half of the ramekin with the vinegar, stretch film over the top. Poke little holes in the saran wrap. Place near infected area. After a day or two, you will be unable to count how many of those little ******* are dead in there. Rinse and repeat when it starts to get too full. I have probably killed millions with this little death pit. These are a gimmick, stay away. Especially for fruit flies. Not sure how well they work for mosquitos.

title: Apple cider vinegar works better than this!
body: This doesn’t even deserve 1 star. It’s officially been 24hrs since it was delivered and plugged in. It has been in my kitchen, directly next to the fruit that sits on the counter. I currently have an INSANE amount of fruit flies due to “someone” leaving an opened applesauce in the pantry…. I did a test. I put a small medicine cap filled with apple cider vinegar and Dawn dish soap in a separate portion of my house, where I have seen the least activity of fruit flies. The kitchen area is over run with fruit flies. The photos speak for themselves. For fun, I even took a piece of cardboard and did a layer of Elmer school glue right after I plugged in the blue light. Again, the photos speak for themselves. You see how many fruit flies were trapped by the Elmers glue makeshift trap, in the short time it took to dry, compared to this $20 piece of junk. I truly don’t understand how this has so many great reviews. Photo 1 is the small cap filled with ACV and Dawn (the cloudiness are drowned fruit flies). Photo 2 is the school glue, photo 3 is this product 🙄🤨 I will be returning this!

title: It didn't work as expected.
body: I recently purchased the ZEVO Fly Trap after reading numerous glowing reviews that touted its effectiveness in catching flies. With summer in full swing and the usual influx of pesky insects, I was eager to try out this product. Unfortunately, my experience has been far from the exceptional results I had hoped for. Performance: Over the course of a week, I placed the ZEVO Fly Trap in a strategic location where I typically see a lot of fly activity. To my disappointment, it only caught one fly during that entire time. I had expected a much higher catch rate based on the reviews I had read, which made me question the reliability of those testimonials. Expectations vs. Reality: Given the rave reviews, I anticipated a significant reduction in the fly population in my home. Instead, I found myself swatting flies as usual, with the trap seemingly doing little to help. It’s puzzling how others have had such positive experiences while mine was lackluster at best. Conclusion: While the ZEVO Fly Trap may work for some, my experience has been disappointing. I had high hopes based on the exceptional reviews, but the results did not match the hype. If you’re considering this product, I recommend tempering your expectations and perhaps exploring other options if you’re dealing with a significant fly problem. For me, it’s back to the drawing board in the search for an effective fly control solution.

title: In FIVE days it only caught THREE FLIES - Sending it back
body: I am underwhelmed. In FIVE days it only caught THREE flies. The old fashioned ugly-ass fly strips that are coated with the sticky attractant are just a few dollars for a pack of ten that will last several months and they work better than this useless contraption. Very disappointed. All those 5 stars Amazon reviews must be AI generated? Right now I am sitting on my couch in my living room and there are 8 flies buzzing around me driving me CRAZY. Flies are strongly attracted to carbon dioxide that humans breathe out. They will land on us and eat the dead skin cells and sebum on our skin. No matter how much you swat them away they keep coming back. This gadget looked impressive - the blue light is supposed to attract the fly into the sticky trap BUT THAT DOES NOT WORK except in a very minimal ineffectual manner. Seriously! For what this costs to only catch THREE flies in FIVE days is unacceptable. I did better putting out a dish of vinegar with sugar as an attractant but put a tbsp of Dawn dish soap in the bowl - that attraxts the fly and they drown. I'm sending it back for a full refund. I also bought a box of refills and that goes back to Amazon. BADLY DONE! 1 star is too high a rating

body: DO NOT waste your money on this product. I have had two of these since September. The picture is after 6 months. There is nothing but cat hair. I always have an issue when I bring home fruit. I usually wash it but that still does not guarantee no gnats. The best way to get rid of gnats is this. I get a quart bottle of cider vinegar. I put 2tbs of sugar, and 5 drops of dish detergent in the bottle. The detergent changes the viscosity of the mix so once they get in they can't get out. Put a piece of saran wrap on the top and hold it in place with a rubber band. Poke 3 or 4 holes in the top and leave it next to the source or close to the area that is infested with gnats. I thought these would be great as my wife hates the vinegar smell. But they do nothing. It's a great night light, but I have fairy lights for night lights. Don't waste your time or money on this product if you are trying to kill gnats. I don't know how this product works with mosquitoes, as I have no mosquito problem in the house.

title: Does not work.
body: In all fairness, I bought the main Zevo plug-in piece from a box store, because it only had one sticky sheet. My wife and I wanted to try it before we invested in any of the refills. We plugged it in to the garage outlet, about 3 ft from the door into the house. We left it there almost 2 weeks. In that time, it caught 3 (yes, three) flies, 1 wasp and a bunch of gnats. My wife contacted Zevo and complained about the poor performance. They said it should really be plugged in in the kitchen, as the flies are (supposed to be) attracted to the blue light. title: Attracts some but not all species. Liquid bait traps are better.
body: About a month ago I suddenly and inexplicably noticed dozens of tiny little bugs flying around in my kitchen. Absolutely disgusting. Neurotic cleaning ensued, and, eventually, the flies dissipated, but not as quickly as I would have liked. I decided to purchase some fly traps to put my thumb on the scale. These light traps appeared to be working at first. They were definitely catching some flies, but the total number of flies was not visibly decreasing. Then I noticed that the flies stuck on the trap looked different than the ones still flying around. The light was definitely attracting one species of fly, but another species seemed completely unaffected. They were a lighter color, whereas the flies in the trap were darker. After a few days, the darker flies were gone, and the lighter flies appeared to have expanded their population to take advantage of their absence. So anyways, I suppose whether these traps work for you will depend on what species of fly you’re dealing with. For me, these traps were ineffective. I then purchased some of those liquid bait traps that look like tiny little apples, and they worked incredibly well. The liquid comes in a tiny little bottle and cannot be purchased separately, which is asinine, but apple cider vinegar with a little dish soap appears to work just as well as the bait that comes with the trap. I tried using apple cider vinegar with dish soap in a DIY trap before purchasing some traps, but this was not effective. I think it was too difficult for the flies to get to the bait. The premade traps with DIY bait appears to be the best of both worlds.

title: I wouldn’t purchase again
body: I’ve seen ads for this product for a while so it immediately came to mind as a solution when we started having a fruit fly problem. I placed it where I had seen most of the fruit flies hanging out and it did catch a few, but I was a little disappointed that it wasn’t making much of a dent in the population. Something else I should have considered before purchasing was how brightly the blue light shines from this device. We avoid blue light around bedtime and dim the lights in our house in the evenings as we get ready to sleep and so this didn’t fit with my personal sleep hygiene preferences - but that’s honestly my fault for not thinking through how this product works before purchasing it. After giving Zevo a chance for a few days I decided to try the old apple cider vinegar in a jar with tiny holes poked in the lid method. The apple cider jar was the clear winner and captured at least 3-4 times more in a single night than the Zivo had in days. The homemade method was much cheaper too. If I could go back and do it all over again I would just do the jar trick and save money by not purchasing this product.

title: Nice-looking, simple concept but poor design
body: The concept of these traps is simple and typically very effective at catching flying insects. We've used similar products with excellent results and I am fairly sure these would have also worked quite well. However, I ended up returning these and buying the Safer Home traps, which looks very similar to these because these have a (completely unnecessary IMO) ON/OFF button on them that does not remember what state it was in, so every single time the power goes out, even for the shortest amount of time, I have to go around and press the button on every trap to turn them back on. Seriously people, why??? It's an insect trap and its job is to be on catching insects, so why overcomplicate things by adding an ON/OFF button? And if you really must have an ON/OFF button, make it mechanical, so it will stay in the current state. Initially when I plugged the first one in, I thought it didn't work, then realized it had that button, which is not that noticeable (and you know I didn't read the instructions). Also, while I still think these would work, I feel that the LEDs on this trap are not as effective as those on the Safer Home units and these seemed to light up the room more, even though the LEDs don't seem as bright (I think they are a slightly lower wavelength of UV than the Safer Home units use. In any case, I cannot recommend this product due to the above, as there are other choices that are better designed and work exceptionally well in the same price range.

title: May catch 5/100 in weeks. Another ripoff.
body: Ah, the FlyTrap—my new favorite kitchen décor! I bought it in a moment of desperation, convinced that it would be my knight in shining armor against the relentless army of flies and maggots invading my space. Little did I know, the commercial was just a well-crafted fairy tale, complete with staged videos of the trap looking like a five-star buffet for flies. Weeks later, and not a single fly has even glanced at my sticky little contraption. It’s like the ultimate fly rejection therapy! I can practically hear them laughing as they buzz past, enjoying their freedom while my FlyTrap collects dust. So, if you're looking for a decorative piece that screams "I tried," then by all means, go ahead and purchase this glorified paperweight. Just don't expect any actual results—unless you count the satisfaction of watching it sit there, utterly useless. Cheers to false advertising!

body: I purchased the FVOAI Fruit Fly Trap in March 2025. It worked at first, then sat powered off for about four months. Today did not turn on. After checking with its own, I tried multiple USB adapters and cables; pressing the power button does nothing—no lights, no response. The bigger issue is support. The email listed on the brand’s site (contact at thefvoai dot com ) bounced (Gmail delivery failure), and the phone number on their site did not connect to a working support line. There was no support contact in the Amazon listing or inside the box brochure—even though the brochure promises: “If you Experience ny Issues with your device this (one yera period) we will be more than happy to replace it free of charge.” I had to hunt down their website just to try contacting them—and even that didn’t work. I understand products can fail. But a warranty is only as good as the ability to reach the company. I’ve wasted time troubleshooting and chasing dead contacts. If FVOAI provides a real channel and resolves this, I will update. Until then, consider the risk that you may be on your own if something goes wrong.

title: Doesn't really work for fruit flies
body: Every year we have a fruit fly issue at our cottage in Northern MI. There are many orchards and vineyards in the area and no matter how careful we are, we get some fruit flies each season. This year we happened to be at the cottage when we had a big outbreak. After a week of temps in the mid 80s, we had a weather shift, dropping the overnight temps into the low 60s with very little wind. The next morning fruit does were everywhere, presumably drawn to the heat of the house. They were outside, inside, everywhere. We rent this cottage and the UV trap had already been use for two weeks before we arrived. There were a few random insects but nothing terribly impressive. When the fruit flies hit, I put out several traditional bait traps. The photos show the difference. At the time of the photos, the UV trap had been in steady operation for 3 weeks. The red/ fruit trap was only out for 2 hours!!! I'm not kidding and not exaggerating. This is two hours. There are two issues here. (1) Fruit flies don't seem particularly attracted to UV light and (2) the suction of the fan isn't remotely adequate.

We are unsure what caused it to be this way since we only ever turn it on/off and leave it in one place. It’s too noisy to use. I tried searching for a way to contact FVOAI through Amazon and their website to see if I could get it replaced, but it doesn’t look like there’s any way to do so after the initial 30-day window. Unfortunate since we really liked this product but now are unable to continue using it due to the sudden malfunction.
